llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (local LAN UDP peer discovery and messaging); there are no hidden endpoints or unrelated credential requests, but it does open a UDP socket and exposes a hostname-derived agent ID so users should review and restrict use on untrusted networks.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (local UDP messaging) align with the included code and registered tools (udp_discover, udp_send, udp_receive, udp_approve_peer, etc.). Required binary is node — appropriate for the TypeScript/Node plugin.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and CLAUDE/README clearly describe broadcasting discovery pings and exchanging plaintext JSON messages over UDP. The runtime instructions explicitly require user approval before trusting peers and warn not to send secrets — appropriate but relies on correct user behavior. The plugin will reveal a hostname-derived agentId in messages, which is a privacy detail worth noting.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry shows no install spec but SKILL.md/package.json reference installing from npm or a GitHub repo (https://github.com/turfptax/openclaw-udp-messenger.git). Downloading and executing plugin code from a GitHub repo is common but carries the usual supply-chain risk; the code included in the package appears readable and not obfuscated.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, secrets, or unrelated credentials. The only sensitive-ish information emitted is agentId (hostname + random hex) which is sent to peers — consistent with purpose but a privacy consideration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no system config paths requested. The plugin registers a hook (check-inbox) to prompt about unread messages before stopping — reasonable for this capability. Autonomous invocation of registered tools is allowed by platform default (not flagged alone).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: open a UDP socket, discover peers on the LAN, and exchange plaintext JSON messages. Before installing, consider: 
- Only install from a source you trust (verify the GitHub repo or npm package and its history). 
- The plugin broadcasts on the LAN and includes a hostname-derived agentId in messages — avoid on untrusted networks. 
- Use trustMode="always-confirm" if you don't trust the local network; only approve known peers. 
- Never instruct the agent to send secrets or file contents to peers; approving a peer lets them receive future messages in approve-once mode. 
- If you need extra safety, run the plugin in an isolated environment or restrict it with firewall rules (limit port 51337 to a controlled VLAN). 
Overall this is internally coherent but network and privacy risks are inherent to its function — proceed only if you understand and accept those risks.
